Busan Fireworks Festival 2026: How K-Pop Stars Like Stray Kids Are Helping South Korea Turn Fandom Into Tourism
 The annual fireworks celebration will take place around Gwangalli Beach, Igidae, and Dongbaekseom Island.
 By Samhati Bhattacharjya 
 November 2, 2026 18:37 +08 
 The 21st edition of the Busan Fireworks Festival is scheduled to run from 1 pm to 8 pm on Nov. 7. 
 Wikimediacommons (Representational Image) 
 South Korea's entertainment industry is increasingly influencing how international audiences experience the country, with K-pop becoming an important gateway to destinations beyond Seoul.
 Busan, the country's second-largest city, is now looking to capitalize on that global interest by combining its cultural attractions, major public events, and celebrity-led tourism campaigns.
 As the city prepares for its 21st Busan Fireworks Festival on Nov. 7, its growing connection with the Korean entertainment industry offers an interesting look at how music fandom can create opportunities for regional tourism.
 The annual fireworks celebration will take place around Gwangalli Beach, Igidae, and Dongbaekseom Island. While the festival is not a K-pop concert, its timing provides an opportunity to examine a larger development in South Korea: the growing relationship between entertainment, international fandom, and destination marketing.
 Busan is no longer relying exclusively on its beaches, food culture, and coastal attractions to draw visitors. It is also exploring how the international popularity of Korean artists can encourage fans to discover the city for themselves.
 Busan Fireworks Festival 2026: What to Expect?
 The 21st edition of the Busan Fireworks Festival is scheduled to run from 1 pm to 8 pm on Nov. 7. The program will combine daytime entertainment with an evening fireworks spectacle featuring international participation and a large-scale display over the city's coastline.
 According to the official festival schedule, daytime activities will include busking performances, chalk art, scratch art, and interactive booths. The Republic of Korea Air Force's Black Eagles aerobatic team is also scheduled to perform an air show at 4 pm.
 The evening program will begin with a fireworks prologue at 6 pm, followed by the opening ceremony. An international guest fireworks presentation representing China is scheduled for 7 pm, while the main Busan Multi-Fireworks Show will take place from 7:25 pm to 7:55 pm. A closing fireworks presentation will conclude the event.
 The main display will feature large-scale fireworks effects, including Niagara fireworks and 25-inch aerial shells. Organizers have designed the event around the combination of music, lighting, and visual storytelling, making the surrounding coastal landscape an important part of the experience.
 The festival is expected to attract a substantial audience. Busan authorities have announced plans to deploy more than 7,000 personnel for crowd management and public safety, with attendance expected to exceed one million.
 Stray Kids' Busan Tourism Video Crosses 10 Million Views
 One of the clearest examples of K-pop's growing influence on regional tourism comes from a recent campaign featuring Stray Kids.
 The Korea Tourism Organization's BIAS (Be In Artists' Scenes) campaign, developed in collaboration with JYP Entertainment , uses the popularity of K-pop artists to introduce international audiences to destinations across South Korea.
 Its Busan installment features Stray Kids visiting attractions in the city, including Songdo Beach, Bupyeong Kkangtong Market, and Gamcheon Culture Village. The campaign also has a personal connection through member I.N., who is from Busan.
 On Sept. 28, KBS World reported that the promotional video had surpassed 10 million views. The campaign was designed to encourage international fans to visit the locations featured in the content rather than simply watch their favorite artists explore them online.
 The Korea Tourism Organization has also worked with travel platform Klook to promote itineraries and travel benefits connected to the featured attractions.
 This approach offers an interesting example of how entertainment marketing can move beyond traditional promotional videos. Instead of simply introducing a destination through conventional tourism advertising, the campaign uses familiar artists and locations to create a connection with potential visitors.
 How Busan is Using BTS and K-Pop to Build Its Tourism Identity? 
 Stray Kids is not the only group whose popularity has helped Busan attract international attention.
 BTS has a particularly strong connection with the city through members Jimin and Jungkook , both of whom have hometown ties to Busan. The group's 2022 concert, Yet to Come in Busan, also brought significant international attention to the destination.
 In June 2026, Busan Metropolitan City launched its INTO K-POP, INTO BUSAN tourism campaign alongside major entertainment events, including BTS' ARIRANG world tour concerts on June 12 and 13 and the Busan One Asia Festival on June 27 and 28.
 The initiative was designed to encourage concertgoers to explore more of the city, including its beaches, food destinations, nightlife, and cultural attractions.
 Rather than treating concerts as isolated events, the campaign connected them with local businesses, tourism experiences, promotional activities, and visitor services.
 Its five-stage concept, including Welcome, Taste, Experience, Stay, and Share, was intended to take visitors through different aspects of the city, from their arrival to the experiences they could share after returning home.
 This strategy demonstrates how Busan is attempting to make entertainment-related travel more valuable to the wider local economy.
 A visitor arriving for a concert may spend money on accommodation, restaurants, transportation, shopping, and sightseeing. By encouraging fans to extend their stay, the city can potentially distribute the economic benefits across several sectors.
 Why South Korea Wants K-Pop Fans to Explore Beyond Seoul?
 Seoul remains the center of South Korea's entertainment industry, with major agencies, music production facilities, television networks, and concert venues concentrated in and around the capital.
 However, the country's regional tourism authorities have increasingly recognized that international interest in Korean entertainment could benefit destinations outside Seoul.
 The appeal of K-pop is not limited to album releases or live performances. Fans often develop an interest in the places associated with their favorite artists, including hometowns, restaurants, filming locations, and cultural attractions.
 The Stray Kids campaign demonstrates how that interest can be translated into destination-focused promotional content. Its use of I.N.'s connection to Busan gives international audiences an additional reason to explore the city.
 The Korea Tourism Organization's approach also suggests that digital engagement can become a starting point for actual travel experiences. By connecting online content with bookable itineraries and location-based promotions, the campaign attempts to bridge the gap between watching an artist's travel experience and creating one independently.
 Can Cultural Festivals and K-Pop Create Sustainable Tourism Boom? 
 The Busan Fireworks Festival and the city's K-pop tourism initiatives represent two different approaches to attracting visitors, but they share an important objective: encouraging people to experience the destination rather than simply consume promotional content.
 The fireworks festival highlights Busan's geographical and cultural identity through a large-scale public celebration. K-pop campaigns, meanwhile, use the international popularity of artists to introduce the city to audiences who may already have an emotional connection with Korean entertainment.
 Combining these approaches could help Busan build a broader international tourism identity.
 However, attracting attention is only one part of the process. Sustained tourism growth depends on practical factors such as transportation, accommodation, visitor facilities, local business participation, and the quality of experiences available throughout the year.
 There is also a distinction between generating millions of online views and converting that attention into actual international visits. The Stray Kids campaign's reported 10 million views demonstrate its digital reach, but longer-term tourism results will depend on whether audiences follow through with travel plans.
 Busan's Global Ambitions Extend Beyond the Fireworks 
 The Nov. 7 celebration will put Busan's coastline in the international spotlight, but the city's wider ambitions extend beyond one night of fireworks.
 Its collaborations with K-pop artists, tourism organizations, and local businesses indicate an effort to connect South Korea's entertainment appeal with regional destinations and visitor experiences.
 The distinction is important: the Busan Fireworks Festival is not being promoted as a BTS or Stray Kids concert, and no such idol appearance is confirmed in its official program. Instead, the festival is part of a wider cultural calendar that gives international visitors another reason to discover the city.
 As South Korea continues to benefit from the global popularity of its music, television, and entertainment, Busan's approach offers an example of how regional destinations can participate in that momentum.
 For the entertainment industry, the potential extends beyond streaming numbers, concert attendance, and merchandise sales. K-pop's influence can also shape travel decisions, introduce audiences to local culture, and create opportunities for businesses far removed from the music industry.
 The fireworks may be the biggest attraction in Busan this November, but the city's larger ambition is to ensure that international visitors have reasons to return long after the final display fades.
